newsitem.title: USA: Chino copper mine labor talks still in recess.
newsitem.headline: Chino copper mine labor talks still in recess.

text.p: Labor talks at Phelps Dodge Corp's Chino mine in New Mexico were still in recess as employees reauthorised the United Steelworkers of America's negotiating committee to call a strike if the company fails to budge, a union official said.
Robert Guadiana, USWA lead negotiator at Chino, said the union was waiting for information from the company regarding proposals which have been passing back and forth between the two sides.
No date for further talks has been fixed.
Guadiana said the "slightly irritated" unionized employees met Monday and voted unanimously again in favor of striking if talks with Phelps did not progress.

"That simply authorises the negotiating committee, if the company does not move, to take whatever action is necessary. If does not mean stike, but if necessary they can do that," Guadiana said. "Hopefully there will not be one."
Union member employees have been without a contract since June 30.
Talks last Friday failed to break the deadlock.
Late August Phelps' made what it termed its final offer - a four-year deal without pay rise.
Guadiana said current discussions focused on a six-year deal with disagreement over how much of a pay hike, if any, there should be in each year of the contract.
